entries.title: Start Here
entries.summary: Read this first if you played EC4

blocks.text: This book was copied out afresh from an older research book, and a good many pages were changed along the way. If you knew the old book, read this first, so your memory of it doesn't send you the wrong way.

This chapter is for players who knew the 1.12 original, EssentialCraft 4 Unofficial. It covers where the old things are now, which rules changed and what was removed. If this is your first time with the mod, skip the whole chapter; everything the main line needs is written in its own chapter.
The biggest differences

items.text: Machines no longer dig or place blocks in the world. The Magical Quarry, Activators, Breakers and the Replanter are gone. For ores, use the {item:essentialcraft5:ley_projector}, which projects them inside the machine and leaves the ground alone.
Machines no longer dig or place blocks in the world. The Magical Quarry, Activators, Breakers and the Replanter are gone.

items: Anything that can hurt or affect other players plays by the rules: before acting, it checks whether players may hurt each other, whether you're on the same team and whether the target stands in someone else's claim. Explosions still happen, but they no longer break blocks.

items.text: The {item:essentialcraft5:mru_coil} is the exception. It guards your home and still zaps intruders in your claim who aren't on its whitelist, even when players can't hurt each other ([[tesla/mru_coil]]).
The {item:essentialcraft5:mru_coil} is the exception. It guards your home and still zaps any player who isn't on its whitelist ([[tesla/mru_coil]]).

items: Baubles go in the Curios slots, and you can wear only one of each kind, so a second copy won't go in ([[from_ec4/how]]).
The research book is now this guide. There are no upgrades to craft, and every page is open from the start. Hold Ctrl over an item's tooltip to jump to the page about it.

items.text: Late-game armor no longer blocks everything while powered. With power, the Void suit blocks melee and projectiles, and the Computer Guy's suit blocks elemental damage as well. In return, both now have real armor points and extra health ([[from_ec4/changed]]).

blocks.text: How to find things

items: Search for the old name: just start typing on the home page, for example “Quarry” or “Magical Inventory Manager”, to find the page in this chapter that mentions it.
Browse by the old book's categories: [[from_ec4/where]] lists renamed and reworked things under the five categories of the original research book.
Click an item name in the tables to jump to the page that covers it now.

blocks.text: Everything below is new in this version and was not in the original. Click a name to jump to the page that covers it.
Machines and items

cells: Takes the place of the old Magical Quarry. It digs nothing, and instead spends MRU to project the ores of this world's rock layers inside the machine
Can be made once you have beaten the holographic projection. It condenses diamonds, emeralds and other vanilla ores out of MRU, and nether stars if you add ESPE as well

Comes in four tiers that turn MRU into energy (FE) and push it into other mods' machines, cables and batteries touching them, plus an infinite tier that needs no MRU. The original didn't work with any other mod

Comes in four tiers that turn MRU into energy (FE) or Botania mana and push it into machines, cables and mana pools touching them, plus an infinite tier that needs no MRU. The original didn't work with any other mod

rows: The infinite MRU source, the infinite ESPE source and a few others. None has a recipe, but once you have one it works in survival. The original had only two creative sources, and they just waited for machines to draw from them
Right-click another player to add them, sneak-right-click to cross yourself off, and put it alone in a crafting grid to wipe it. The original could only add you
Works with a comparator: the fuller it is, the stronger the signal

cells: Sneak-right-click it with an empty hand and it lets go of what it holds, so a mistake can be undone. In the original, whatever you put on stayed there
Sneak-right-click the air while it is working to stop it
Whether night vision is on is saved on you, so it survives relogging and death. In the original it lived only on your own client
Beat the holographic projection without wearing any armor. The original only mentioned it in a code comment

Wearing the full Computer Guy's Suit, switch it on in the terminal ({keybind:key.essentialcraft5.computer_terminal}). Players within {cfg:general.computer_seal.radius} blocks who fought you in the last {cfg:general.computer_seal.combat_window_ticks|sec} lose the effects of everything in their Curios slots. One real hit between you counts as fighting, whoever struck first. Players standing where you can't change blocks, such as someone else's claim, are left alone, and it does nothing in some worlds

Wearing the full Computer Guy's Suit, switch it on in the terminal ({keybind:key.essentialcraft5.computer_terminal}). Other players within {cfg:general.computer_seal.radius} blocks lose the effects of everything in their Curios slots. Teammates, players who may not hurt you and players standing where you can't change blocks, such as someone else's claim, are left alone, and it does nothing in some worlds

An optional machine from the Computer Guy's Suit chapter. Fed with MRU, it stops natural monster spawns within {cfg:machines.force_dome.radius} blocks horizontally. It only covers chunks where whoever placed it may build, and spawners and spawn eggs still work

Chaos, frozen, magic and shade lenses each add an effect when the ray lands: Corrosion (no healing), freezing, dispelling one beneficial effect, and draining health back to you. The original lenses only changed the color, and the shade projection couldn't be made at all. Now the Radiating Chamber makes it
Keep raising your wind relation after the true name is revealed. At {cfg:general.wind.steadfast_points} you can't be knocked back while sneaking
At {cfg:general.wind.deflect_points} relation, projectiles others shoot or throw at you pass straight through, one every {cfg:general.wind.deflect_cooldown_ticks|sec}

Seven books the forebears left in ancient ruins, in Hoanna and on the Inquisitorium Sentinel. Each one you read opens a page in the Ancient Scrolls chapter, and reading them all adds a little MRU corruption and Hoanna radiation resistance for good

Books the forebears left. Five of them can be found in the Overworld, all in ancient ruin chests. Each one you read opens a page in the Ancient Scrolls chapter, and reading all five adds a little MRU corruption resistance for good

rows: Seeds or saplings go in as samples and grow inside the machine on MRU and water. The sample is never used up, and the blocks around it are left alone
Breaks junk such as cobblestone, rotten flesh and feathers into element points, and makes an essence whenever one element has enough
Scans for ores around you and outlines them on your screen only; sneak-right-click to switch modes, and the MRUCU mode points toward a large MRUCU nearby
A pickaxe you can make from Chapter 13 on. It runs on MRU, never breaks, and mines the 3×3 on the face you hit
The pickaxe's partner. Chop one log and the whole natural tree comes down
Set a home point, then hold right-click for a few seconds to go back to it

cells: Your MRU Matrix now has nine ranks. Meet the Codex requirement, gather the offerings and energy, then win a trial at the {item:essentialcraft5:matrix_crucible} to go up one rank. Each rank adds something new, such as storing MRU inside you or the matrix siphon. The main line asks for a breakthrough every few chapters
What an Enrichment Chamber condenses the MRUCU shut inside it into. Breakthroughs from rank 4 on need it. See [[pentacle/condensed]]
Armor earns attunement points as you take hits in it, and weapons as you land hits with them. Once a stage is full, raise it at the Magician Table. Higher stages unlock more

rows: While you wear armor that blocks damage with MRU, a bar left of the hotbar shows how much charge it has left. See [[storage/charging_chamber]]
A new chapter on the monsters and bosses added in this version: where they show up, how to fight them and what they drop. Elites and per-player diminishing drops are covered on its first page
A fourth kind of wind mage that comes out in thunderstorms, shooting gusts and calling lightning
A boss guarding newly generated ancient ruins. It blocks damage with MRU from the ruin's MRUCU and drops an Ancient Core
A boss you call on a Soul Pentacle with a Matrix Conduit. Pour your matrix damage into it and beat it, and the damage is gone

blocks.text: New rules for coils that hit players
The original {item:essentialcraft5:mru_coil} zapped everyone not on its list, the player who placed it included. It now holds back in the ways below; see [[tesla/mru_coil]].

items: Every coil has its own “hit players” switch, and whoever placed it is never zapped.

items.text: Someone who enters its range for the first time gets a warning {cfg:machines.mru_coil.warning_ticks|sec} before it fires.
Players within {cfg:machines.mru_coil.spawn_safe_radius} blocks of the world spawn are left alone.
A player killed by a coil is safe from every coil for {cfg:machines.mru_coil.respawn_grace_ticks|sec} after respawning.

items: When a coil kills someone, the death message names its owner.

blocks.text: Hoanna

cells: An icon left of the hotbar shows your dose and how fast it rises where you stand, and at high doses the screen edges turn dark purple. It isn't a potion effect, so milk, totems and cleansing can't remove it. The original only had a potion effect

rows: In Hoanna, right-click an empty obsidian frame with a {item:essentialcraft5:wind_tablet} to fill it with a Hoanna portal. The original could only convert portals in the Overworld

cells: An Enrichment Chamber that shuts in a full MRUCU condenses it into a Void Core or an MRU Reactor, depending on the chamber's balance. In the original, both came only from ruin chests

Once you are Windbound, the wind voices one wish after another, such as climbing high, chasing the wind or traveling far, and fulfilling one raises your relation. The Wind Tablet only opens the gate after {cfg:general.wind_wish.required} of them, and once you have that many, the wind asks for no more until its true name is revealed

A goat horn imbued with wind. Blown at night, it calls an Archmage and escorts that fight only you, and an Archmage you defeat yourself always drops a Trapped Wind. In the original, getting a Trapped Wind was down to luck
Sets a pair of embers' on-hit effect into any weapon, other mods' weapons included. Each hit that lands costs {cfg:general.ember_inlay.mru_per_hit} MRU and adds no damage

No longer useless against bosses. Instead of halving them, it Bisects them for {cfg:general.divider_gun.boss_mode_ticks|sec}, halving the damage they deal and the healing they receive. Bosses immune to status effects, the vanilla Wither among them, don't get it
Right-click with a creature in your crosshair to lock on: the strike follows it and stops half a second before landing

A projector you can make after beating the Holographic Projection. It casts a holographic double of you, and nearby hostile mobs that are after you or a teammate turn on it until it fades a few seconds later

Chapter 19, the Inquisitorium, which the original only mentioned as a rumor. Decode the Projection's Glitchy Core in a Radiating Chamber by matching its balance, follow the coordinates to a shadow-corrupted land, and light a beacon to summon the Inquisitorium Sentinel. Its attacks echo and its hits add matrix damage, and it drops Inquisitorium Chips

Modules such as Rewind, Phase Anchor and Attraction for the four pieces of the Computer Guy's Suit. Install them at a crafting table, then switch them on and off or take them out in the Computer Terminal
Stand on it and pay ESPE and MRU to wear away matrix damage. It never cures effects
Goes on the leggings. Pushes nearby drops and orbs to your feet, leaving thrown items alone
Goes on the boots. Lets you step straight up taller ledges
Goes on the leggings or boots. No mining slowdown in midair or with your head underwater
Goes on the helmet. Mobs have to come closer before they notice you
Reforged from an Ember Elemental Sword at its highest attunement stage. Every hit adds damage based on the target's max health, and it can strike a ring of enemies at once
The more trades you complete with demons, the better their terms: two prices to choose from, extra experience per trade, and a Captured Soul to make one reroll its prices

A new side chapter on the specialty each kind of land grows, the mana tide and its ley storms, survey maps, abyssal salt, and the camps out in the wilds with nests to clear. In the original, Hoanna had only ruins and chests

Every kind of land, and the catacombs, has monsters of its own, eight in all, and they drop aberrant residue ([[bestiary/overview|Bestiary]]). The original Hoanna only had the monsters of an Overworld plain

rows: Vaults under the desert and the Dreadlands that open only when four drops are set down in the order on the stele, with an {item:essentialcraft5:elder_remnant} for everyone who opens one
Air domes on the floor of the Hoanna Sea, whose altar calls up the [[bestiary/abyss_tyrant|Abyssal Tidelord]]
Ruined Inquisitorium grounds in the Shadow Corrupted Land, flat and open, a good place to light the beacon
A guard at the center of each town ruin, one per town
A third thing an Enrichment Chamber can collapse into, built near the Shadow Corrupted Land with Umbral Crystals inside
Sworn to a demon for Umbral Crystals once your Demonic Renown reaches {cfg:general.demon.standing.oath}
The final boss, summoned with a Calamity Beacon; beat it for the Calamity Remnant that takes you to matrix rank 9

blocks.text: This guide is new as well. Hold Ctrl over an item's tooltip to open the page about it ([[from_ec4/how]]).

blocks.title: Why
blocks.text: Most of these changes come from three rules: leave other players' claims, pets and machines alone, don't slow the game down, and keep the Overworld from getting crowded. The original rarely thought about these, and that caused trouble once many people played together.
These are things the original had and this version doesn't. Most of them ignored land claims, slowed the game down or made mob farms too easy. Whatever could be kept in another form was kept.

entries.title: Done Differently
entries.summary: Curios, tags, the guide and keys

blocks.text: This page isn't about rules but about how things are done. The mods and 1.12 mechanics the original relied on don't exist in 1.20.1, so other ways have replaced them.
Bauble slots: from Baubles to Curios

In the original, baubles went into the Baubles mod's slots; now they go into Curios slots. Open your inventory and click the curios button next to your character, or just press {keybind:key.curios.open.desc}.

rows: The ten charms, amulets and pendants, the Wind Mage's Talisman, the Portable Matrix Destructor
All the rings, plus soul storage (Soul Shard up to Matter Of Eternity)

cells: Its form is rolled when the chest is opened and decides the slot

items: Baubles also had head, body and charm slots. Nothing from the original went there, and this mod doesn't use them either.
As in the original, there are at least two ring slots; if another mod or the modpack adds more, you get those too.
Only one of each kind. Two identical rings stacked in the original, but now the second one won't go in ([[baubles/finding]]).

blocks.text: Ore dictionary became tags
In 1.12 the ore dictionary let the same material from different mods count as one, so every mod's copper ingot was a “copper ingot”. In 1.20 tags do much the same job.

Mangrove, cherry, cornflowers and lilies of the valley were added to the {item:essentialcraft5:mithriline_furnace} conversions ([[mithriline/conversions]]).
The world now goes down to −64, and a {item:essentialcraft5:moon_well} at height 0 or below runs at full rate ([[crystal/moon_well]]).

blocks.text: From metadata to block states

Blocks have had no metadata since 1.13. The {item:essentialcraft5:metadata_manager} now reads a number from the block in front of it, such as crop age or cake bites, and ripe wheat gives 7. When that block changes, it follows by itself, with no manual block update needed ([[automation/metadata_manager]]).
